items.summary: Disposition: evidence_needed. Risk severity is high for go-live and security-sensitive releases, and medium for ordinary reversible growth. Fleet-doctor has no run or findings; operations deploy, uptime, and error sweeps have no results. Authentication and access boundaries, secrets handling, runtime isolation, release/deploy controls, dependency provenance, monitoring, incident readiness, broader TLS evidence, data-exposure controls, and security.txt/disclosure readiness remain unevidenced. Compliance is only a technical baseline: 36 pass, 19 fail, and 6 unknown. Decision: keep private-launch and security-sensitive release gates unchanged. Permit ordinary reversible growth only when it adds no credentials, permissions, dependencies, data collection, or cross-site behavior. This is not evidence of compromise, certification, or a clean bill of health.

Retain the existing consolidated security evidence matrix and do not create duplicate telemetry or security work. Use authorized metadata and retained artifacts only to document authentication, access boundaries, secrets, isolation, release controls, dependency provenance, TLS, data exposure, monitoring, incident response, and disclosure readiness. Do not retrieve credentials, access private containers, exploit targets, modify permissions or configuration, deploy, add dependencies, or clear security-sensitive release gates.

Security evidence is incomplete across access control, secrets, isolation, release/deploy controls, dependencies, TLS, monitoring, incident handling, data exposure, and disclosure readiness. Retain the existing read-only evidence bundle; do not send outreach, change production, enable tracking, add credentials, or add dependencies.
